expected_failures.pad_right (131072|196608|16777183|167771: Beryl refuses a handshake message over its 64 KiB limit (plan §4) from the message header with illegal_parameter, before reading the body; tlsfuzzer expects decode_error. Both refuse.

scripts.arguments_reason: Beryl answers every update_requested KeyUpdate that arrives before its next application data with a single KeyUpdate, as BoringSSL does and BoGo requires (KeyUpdate-Requested); RFC 9846 §4.6.3 allows either.

expected_failures.^app data split, conversation with KeyUp: The script sends part of an HTTP request, then a KeyUpdate asking for an answer, and waits for that answer before sending the rest. Beryl, like BoringSSL, sends the answering KeyUpdate before its next application data record (RFC 9846 §4.6.3), and the example server writes nothing until the request is complete, so the script times out. The answer arrives first in every probe that lets the server reply.

expected_failures.32715: The ClientHello with 32,715 signature schemes is over Beryl's 64 KiB handshake message limit (plan §4), refused with illegal_parameter.

expected_failures.downgrade to TLS 1\\.2: Needs a TLS 1.2 fallback. Beryl speaks TLS 1.3 only; TLS 1.2 is milestone B6.

expected_failures.^After NewSessionTicket$: The script's ClientHello offers no psk_key_exchange_modes, and Beryl sends tickets only to a client that lists psk_dhe_ke (RFC 9846 §4.2.9), so the NewSessionTicket this probe waits for never comes.

expected_failures.TLS 1\\.2: Needs TLS 1.2 sessions. Beryl speaks TLS 1.3 only; TLS 1.2 is milestone B6.
expected_failures.PSK_ONLY: Beryl refuses psk_ke: every resumption runs a fresh ECDHE exchange (plan §2), so a psk_ke-only offer gets a full handshake.

expected_failures.to 1\\.2$: Expects a fallback to TLS 1.2. Beryl speaks TLS 1.3 only; TLS 1.2 is milestone B6.
expected_failures.TLS 1\\.2: Expects TLS 1.2. Beryl speaks TLS 1.3 only; TLS 1.2 is milestone B6.
expected_failures.to 1\\.1$: Expects a fallback to TLS 1.1. Beryl speaks TLS 1.3 only.
expected_failures.in client hello legacy field$: Without supported_versions this ClientHello asks for TLS 1.2, which Beryl does not speak; TLS 1.2 is milestone B6.

scripts.arguments_reason: -a handshake_failure: with no group in common Beryl sends handshake_failure (RFC 9846 §4.1.1). --relaxed: a client that also speaks TLS 1.2 may list TLS 1.2 curves beside secp256r1, and Beryl negotiates secp256r1.

expected_failures.secp384r1_sha384|secp521r1_sha512|brainp: The script expects a server key for each curve; the server holds a P-256 key, and Beryl signs with P-256, Ed25519 and RSA (plan §2). It refuses the other schemes with handshake_failure.

expected_failures.^ed448 only$: The script expects an Ed448 key too; Ed448 is not implemented, and with only ed448 offered Beryl refuses with handshake_failure.
